evidence.quote: Cohen syndrome (OMIM No. # 216550) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by homozygous mutation in the vacuolar protein sorting 13 homolog B (VPS13B) gene on chromosome 8q22.2.
evidence.supports: Explicit, non-hedged causal attribution of Cohen syndrome to (homozygous) VPS13B mutation stated as established knowledge in the Abstract background.

evidence.quote: Mutation in the 13B vacuolar sorting protein gene, vacuolar protein sorting 13 homolog B (VPS13B) (8q22-8q23) gene, which is the only gene responsible for Cohen syndrome [3-5].
evidence.supports: Cited background statement that VPS13B mutation is the (only) gene responsible for Cohen syndrome. Sentence is grammatically incomplete but the attribution is explicit.

evidence.quote: To date, about 200 VPS13B mutations have been reported in nearly 1,000 cases of Cohen syndrome [10], of which about five cases have been genetically diagnosed in China [10,11].
evidence.supports: Cited background population-level report of VPS13B mutations in Cohen syndrome patients, used as disease-relevant fact (mutation spectrum).

conditions.population: nearly 1,000 Cohen syndrome cases (as stated; not verified)

evidence.quote: To date, more than 200 mutations of VPS13B have been reported in over 1,000 Cohen syndrome patients.
evidence.supports: Abstract restatement of E3 (background population report).

evidence.quote: Although this variant (cases 1 and 2) 8q22, NM_017890.4 Intron38 c.6940+1G > T in the VPS13B gene had been detected in patients with Cohen syndrome [7], the deletion of exon 3-19 and Exon56 c10334_10335del of VPS13B gene could constitute complex heterozygous mutations that cause Cohen syndrome with mutation in Intron38 c.6940+1G > T.
evidence.supports: Background: c.6940+1G>T previously detected in Cohen syndrome patients [7]. Present cases: authors attribute Cohen syndrome in the two patients to compound heterozygous VPS13B variants ('could constitute ... that cause'); modal 'could' noted.

conditions.zygosity: compound heterozygous (trans; parental origin per Figures 2-5 captions)

evidence.quote: We found two novel compound heterozygous variants in the VPS13B gene that can induce Cohen syndrome.
evidence.supports: Case-level disease-specific attribution of the patients' Cohen syndrome to VPS13B compound heterozygous variants (R9: supports association, not automatically causal).

evidence.quote: These two mutations were graded in relevant mutation interpretation guidelines by the ACMG as pathogenic.
evidence.supports: ACMG 'pathogenic' classification of detected variants in Case 2; label alone does not establish disease relation (R3); kept as observational context.

evidence.quote: This mutation was graded in relevant mutation interpretation guidelines by the American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) as pathogenic. Heterozygotic deletion of exon 3-19 of the VPS13B gene was also revealed.
evidence.supports: Detection and ACMG classification of VPS13B variants in Case 1; descriptive.

evidence.quote: In addition, in Cohen syndrome neutrophils, the SERPINB1 gene, which encodes a critical component of neutrophil survival, is significantly reduced, leading to excessive apoptosis of neutrophils, which is a possible cause of neutropenia [16].
evidence.supports: Cited background report that SERPINB1 (expression) is significantly reduced in neutrophils of Cohen syndrome patients: an explicit disease-specific expression association. The hedge ('possible cause') applies to the neutropenia link, not to the reduction in Cohen syndrome.

evidence.quote: The possible mechanism of VPS13B causing neutropenia is related to increased neutrophil apoptosis and decreased SerpinB1 expression, which is a critical component of neutrophil survival [15].
evidence.supports: Proposed mechanism linking VPS13B to neutropenia via SerpinB1 expression; neutropenia is an auxiliary phenotype. Does not state a SERPINB1-Cohen syndrome relation by itself.

evidence.quote: According to previous research reports, there is no clear correlation between severity of the disorder and variant [1,12].
evidence.supports: Background: no clear genotype (variant)-severity correlation in Cohen syndrome. Different question (severity vs variant type) from gene-disease association; does not negate VPS13B-Cohen syndrome.

evidence.quote: Cohen syndrome is a clinically heterogeneous disease with extensive and variable clinical manifestations, such as myopia, retinal dystrophy, and heart disease [14,15].
evidence.supports: Lists retinal dystrophy and heart disease as manifestations of Cohen syndrome; no gene is named in the sentence and no gene-manifestation link is stated.

evidence.quote: Cohen syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disease characterized by intellectual disabilities
evidence.supports: Hierarchy basis: Cohen syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disease. No gene stated.

evidence.quote: The probable cause of developmental retardation is that VPS13B gene mutation leads to the reduction of coding protein which is a Golgi-enhanced scaffold protein that helps to maintain the structure and function of the Golgi complex.
evidence.supports: Hedged mechanism for developmental retardation (auxiliary phenotype); no citation.

evidence.quote: The variation was predicted to be pathogenic by related software, and they have not been reported.
evidence.supports: In-silico pathogenicity prediction and novelty claim (abstract).

claims.reason: Case-level disease-specific attribution of the patients' Cohen syndrome to VPS13B compound heterozygous variants (b0066, b0071). Per R9 a case attribution supports association, not automatically causal; 'can induce'/'cause' wording not upgraded.

pairs.reason: Supported. Display type causal from background claim C1 (R3 priority; not a reliability ranking). Study's own contribution (C3) is a case attribution supporting association only, so source_scope of the selected causal claim is 背景引用. Background note of no clear variant-severity correlation (E11) concerns a different endpoint and does not conflict.

'neurodevelopmental disease' appears only as the superclass of Cohen syndrome (b0010). R7: relations are not propagated upward through hierarchy; no direct VPS13B-neurodevelopmental disease statement. 'VPS13B regulates functional neuronal networks [7]' (b0067) is a function statement, not a disease relation.

Retinal dystrophy is listed only as a variable manifestation of Cohen syndrome (b0068) and a monitoring target (b0069); no statement links VPS13B directly to retinal dystrophy and the patients had no ophthalmologic abnormality. Relations to Cohen syndrome are not transferred to its manifestations.
Heart disease is listed only as a variable manifestation of Cohen syndrome (b0068); no VPS13B-heart disease statement; patients had no cardiologic abnormality. Not transferred from Cohen syndrome.
